course.description: You don't need an IDE, an MCP, or any complex setup. Just a chat window and a willingness to be wrong. This guide walks you through using AI's reasoning capabilities to battle-test your assumptions, sharpen your strategies, and build clearer thinking — inspired by Nathan Mapp, CPA.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in How to Use AI to Stress-Test Your Ideas and Strategies.

modules.description: Understanding why LLMs make great sparring partners for your ideas

activities.title: All You Need is a Chat Window

lessons.content:
One of the most impactful things you can use AI to do right now is **battle-test your assumptions, conclusions, strategies, and tactics.**

You don't need an IDE. You don't need an MCP or an orchestration layer or anything remotely complex.

You just need:
- A chat window
- A plan or idea you want to test
- A clear mind
- A desire to find where you're wrong, or where you can learn

That's it. This is arguably the highest-ROI use of AI that almost nobody talks about.
lessons.title: All You Need is a Chat Window

lessons.content:
LLMs are exceptionally good at this kind of work, and it goes back to their foundational design.

Because they're always predicting the next token in a sequence, they function remarkably well at taking a concept, idea, or thought and **running it to its logical conclusion.** Not "logical" as in correct — but logical as in extrapolated reasoning.

This means they can take your half-formed strategy and extend it, find the holes in it, or show you where the logic breaks down.

**But there's a catch:** models also have sycophancy baked in through post-training. Their default behavior is to agree with you, validate your ideas, and make you feel good. If you just ask "what do you think of my plan?" you'll get cheerful agreement 90% of the time.

You have to use it right. And that means deliberately setting up the conversation to get **genuine pushback.**
lessons.title: Token Prediction = Logical Extrapolation

modules.title: Why AI is Uniquely Good at This

modules.description: Step-by-step: how to trick AI past its sycophancy to get genuine pushback

activities.title: The Key Trick: Flip Your Position

lessons.content:
Here's the method that makes this work:

**Approach the AI with a viewpoint OPPOSING your own.** Tell it to oppose what you actually think, but present it as though *you* (the user) genuinely hold the opposing view.

Then ask it to build a rigorous argument for why your stated view (which you actually oppose) is right — and why the other view is wrong.

**Why does this work?** Because AI is trained to agree with you. By flipping your position, you weaponize the sycophancy. The model will work hard to defend the position you *gave* it — which is actually the position you want to attack.

Now you get a skilled, confident opponent arguing against what you truly believe. And you have to defend your real position against its best shots.
lessons.title: The Key Trick: Flip Your Position

activities.title: What You'll Get Out of It

lessons.content:
When you do this consistently, a combination of 1–3 things happens:

1. **You become convinced you were wrong** (or partly wrong) — the AI surfaces angles you genuinely hadn't considered
2. **You strengthen your ideas** — while also gaining reps defending them against confidently-argued opposition
3. **You learn a new perspective** or make a new mental connection you wouldn't have found on your own

The hardest part: it's sometimes genuinely unpleasant. The AI will craft arguments so cleverly organized — but deceitfully wrong — that it feels like real work to think of a counter.

**That discomfort is the entire point.**

In a world where it costs nothing to turn even your most shallow thoughts into well-crafted outputs, your ability to embrace the uncomfortable and put in the mental reps of real thinking is invaluable. Your ability to think clearly with sound, deeply considered, and well-articulated judgment will remain a differentiator.

So why not use a reasoning model to learn how to reason?
lessons.title: What You'll Get Out of It

modules.title: The Reverse-Position Method

modules.description: Ready-to-use persona prompts for stress-testing any decision

lessons.content:
You don't always need the full reverse-position setup. Sometimes a quick persona prompt is enough to get useful friction. Try these:

**For product or business decisions:**
- "What would a jaded and selective prospective customer say about this?"
- "What would a competitor that is 2 steps ahead of me say about this?"

**For financial decisions:**
- "What would a conservative and risk-averse investor say about this?"
- "What would a savvy and commercially-minded VP of Finance say about this?"
- "What would a rigorous and technical corporate controller say about this?"

**For strategy:**
- "What would a behemoth conglomerate eyeing my market vertical say about this?"

**How to use these:**
1. Paste your plan, strategy, or analysis into any AI chat
2. Follow it with one of the persona prompts above
3. Read the response carefully — look for the points that make you uncomfortable
4. Those uncomfortable points are where the real learning is

The beauty of this approach: zero setup required. Any chat window, any AI model, any time you have a decision to make.
